- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines, model overestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 10+ day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to reflect it — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., >0.17) in early window correlate with overestimation — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often ignores sentiment — reduce forecast by 3–6% for 5–10 day horizon.
